akhfash:8-8.t: He said: ﴿وَٱلْخَيْلَ وَٱلْبِغَالَ وَٱلْحَمِيرَ لِتَرْكَبُوهَا﴾, accusative, i.e. "and Allah made the horses, the mules and the donkeys and made them (زِينَةً, an adornment)".

akhfash:9-9.t: He said: ﴿وَمِنْهَا جَآئِرٌ﴾, i.e. "and of the way (السبيل)", because it is feminine in the dialect of the people of the Ḥijāz.

akhfash:12-12.t:
He said: ﴿وَٱلْنُّجُومُ مُسَخَّرَاتٌ﴾, on the sense of "سُخِّرَتْ النُّجُومُ" (the stars were made subservient), or [the accusative] "جَعَلَ النُّجُومَ مُسَخَّراتٍ" (He made the stars subservient). It is permissible to imply a verb other than the first because that implied verb is like the overt one in meaning. The Arabs do what is more extreme than this. The rajaz poet said [and it is the two hundred and thirty-eighth poetic witness]:
تَسْمَعُ فِي أَجْوافِهِنَّ صَرَدَا * وَفِي اليَدَيْنِ جُسْأَةً وَبَدَدا
(You hear a rumbling in their bellies, and [see] in the forelegs stiffness and wide spacing.)
This is in the sense of ﴿وَتَرَى في اليَدَيْنِ الجُسْأَة﴾ (and you see in the forelegs the stiffness) — [which is] dryness — and "البَدَد" [which is] "wide spacing". [Translator's note: the source sets this paraphrase in ﴿…﴾ although it is not a Qur'anic text.]

akhfash:13-13.t: He said: ﴿وَمَا ذَرَأَ لَكُمْ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ مُخْتَلِفاً أَلْوَانُهُ﴾; he says: He created for you and spread out for you.

akhfash:21-21.t: He said: ﴿أَمْواتٌ غَيْرُ أَحْيَآءٍ﴾, by way of tawkīd (emphasis).

akhfash:30-30.t: He said: ﴿وَقِيلَ لِلَّذِينَ ٱتَّقَوْاْ مَاذَا أَنْزَلَ رَبُّكُمْ قَالُواْ خَيْراً﴾: He made "ماذا" have the status of "ما" alone.

akhfash:37-37.t: He said: ﴿إِن تَحْرِصْ﴾, because it is from "حَرَصَ" "يَحْرِصُ".

akhfash:48-48.t:
When you pause on (يَتَفَيّؤُا) you say "يَتَفَيَّأْ", just as you say with the ʿayn "تَتَفَّيعْ" with jussive-like sukūn; and if you wish you may give it a trace of the ḍamma (ishmām) or a slurred vowel (rawm), as you do in "هذا حَجَرُ".
And He said ﴿عَنِ ٱلْيَمِينِ وَٱلْشَّمَآئِلِ سُجَّداً لِلَّهِ وَهُمْ دَاخِرُونَ﴾: He made them masculine though they are not humans, because when He described them as obedient they resembled rational beings. And He made "اليمين" (the right) apply to the group, like ﴿وَيُوَلُّونَ ٱلدُّبُرَ﴾.

akhfash:49-49.t: He said: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ يَسْجُدُ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلأَرْضِ مِن دَآبَّةٍ﴾, meaning "of the creatures", and made do with the singular, as you say "ما أَتاَنِي من رَجُلٍ" (no man came to me), i.e. none of the men like him came to me.

akhfash:53-53.t: He said: ﴿وَمَا بِكُم مِّن نِّعْمَةٍ فَمِنَ ٱللَّهِ﴾: because (ما) has the status of (من) [i.e. a conditional/relative], He introduced the khabar with fāʾ.

akhfash:67-67.t: He said: ﴿وَمِن ثَمَرَاتِ ٱلنَّخِيلِ وَٱلأَعْنَابِ تَتَّخِذُونَ مِنْهُ سَكَراً وَرِزْقاً حَسَناً﴾ and did not say "مِنها" (from them), because He implied "الشَيْءَ" (something), as though He said "and of them is something from which you take intoxicant".

akhfash:68-68.t: He said: ﴿إِلَىٰ ٱلنَّحْلِ أَنِ ٱتَّخِذِي﴾, in the feminine, in the dialect of the people of the Ḥijāz; others say "هُوَ النَّحْل" (masculine). Likewise every collective plural which differs from its singular only by the hāʾ, such as "البُرُّ" (wheat) and "الشَعِيرُ" (barley), is feminine in their dialect.

akhfash:69-69.t: He said: ﴿ذُلُلاً﴾; its singular is "الذَلُولُ" (tractable), and the plural of "الذَّلُول" is "الذُلُل".

akhfash:72-72.t: He said: ﴿بَنِينَ وَحَفَدَةً﴾; their singular is "الحافِدُ" (grandson, helper).

akhfash:73-73.t: He said: ﴿رِزْقاً مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ شَيْئاً﴾: He made "الشَيْء" a badal (substitute) for "الرِّزْق", and it means "they do not possess any provision, little or much". Some said: "الرِّزْقُ is an action that falls on the thing", meaning "they are not able to provide anything".

akhfash:76-76.t: He said: ﴿أَيْنَمَا يُوَجِّههُّ لاَ يَأْتِ بِخَيْرٍ﴾, because (أينّما) is one of the particles of condition (ḥurūf al-mujāzāt).

akhfash:81-81.t: He said: ﴿مِّنَ ٱلْجِبَالِ أَكْنَاناً﴾; its singular is "الكِنّ" (shelter).

akhfash:91-91.t: He said: ﴿وَأَوْفُواْ بِعَهْدِ ٱللَّهِ﴾. You say "أَوْفَيْتُ بالعَهْد" and "وَفَيْتُ بالعَهْد" (I fulfilled the covenant); and when you say "العَهْدَ" [as a direct object], you say "أَوْفَيْتُ العَهْدَ" with the alif.

akhfash:92-92.t: He said: ﴿أَنكَاثاً﴾; its singular is "النِّكْثُ" (untwisted strand).

akhfash:106-106.t: He said: ﴿مَن كَفَرَ بِٱللَّهِ مِن بَعْدِ إيمَانِهِ إِلاَّ مَنْ أُكْرِهَ وَقَلْبُهُ مُطْمَئِنٌّ بِٱلإِيمَانِ وَلَـٰكِن مَّن شَرَحَ بِالْكُفْرِ صَدْراً فَعَلَيْهِمْ غَضَبٌ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ﴾: [فعليهم غضب] is the khabar (predicate) of His words (وَلَكِنْ مَنْ شَرَحَ); then His words ﴿مَن كَفَرَ بِٱللَّهِ مِن بَعْدِ إيمَانِهِ﴾ entered with it, so He gave a single predicate about them both, since that indicates the meaning.

akhfash:111-111.t: He said: ﴿كُلُّ نَفْسٍ تُجَادِلُ عَن نَّفْسِهَا﴾, because the meaning of (كلُّ نَفْسٍ) is "every human being"; He used the feminine because "النفس" (soul) is treated as feminine and masculine. One says "ما جَاءَتْنِي نَفْسٌ واحدةٌ" and "ما جاءَنِي نَفْسٌ واحدٌ" (not a single soul came to me).

akhfash:116-116.t: He said: ﴿أَلْسِنَتُكُمُ ٱلْكَذِبَ﴾: He made (ما تَصِفُ) [what] their tongues [describe] a noun for the action [a maṣdar], as though He said: "and do not say, because of your tongues' describing, (الكَذِبَ هذا حَلاَلٌ, the lie: this is lawful)". Some read (الكَذِبِ) in the genitive; he says: "and do not say of the lie that your tongues describe". Some read (الكُذُبُ) in the nominative and made (الكُذُبَ) an adjective of "the tongues", as though He said "lying tongues".

akhfash:121-121.t: He said: ﴿شَاكِراً لأَنْعُمِهِ﴾ and He said ﴿فَكَفَرَتْ بِأَنْعُمِ ٱللَّهِ﴾: He made "النِّعْمَة" (favour) plural as "أَنْعُمٍ", as He said ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا بَلَغَ أَشُدُّه﴾, which they claimed is the plural of "الشِدَّة".
